alreadyOpen.title: Orchester is already open
alreadyOpen.description: Another Orchester window is using this data folder. One Orchester opens a data folder at a time, so its projects, runners and agents never run twice.
alreadyOpen.footnote: Switching brings that window to the front and closes this one.
alreadyOpen.unsupported: Switching to that window isn't available on this system yet. Bring it to the front yourself, then close this one.
alreadyOpen.unknownProcess: Orchester can't tell which process has the data folder open, so it can't switch to it. Close this window, then find the other one.

closing.title: Orchester is closing
closing.description: The other Orchester window has closed and still has this data folder while its agents save. Start Orchester again in a few seconds.

noAnswer.title: That window didn't come to the front
noAnswer.description: It may be busy or stuck. This window still doesn't open the data folder.
noAnswer.stepBody: If it stays stuck, end process {{pid}} in Task Manager, then start Orchester again. Its agents stop with it, and their runs are offered for continuing on the next start.

newerData.title: Orchester can't open its data
newerData.reason: The database was written by a newer version of Orchester.
newerData.description: It has data version {{found}}; this build reads up to version {{supported}}. Nothing was changed.
newerData.step: Start the newer Orchester that wrote this data, or install it over this one. This build leaves the file as it is: opening it could damage data it doesn't know.

unreadable.title: Orchester can't read its data
unreadable.reason: The database file is damaged or isn't Orchester's: “{{reason}}”.
unreadable.reasonRefused: The database could not be opened: “{{reason}}”.
unreadable.step: Restore the file from a backup if you have one. Moving it out of the folder lets Orchester start with an empty project list: each project keeps its tasks and runs in its own .orchester folder.
unreadable.stepRefused: Close any other program that has the file open, check that your account can read and write it, then start Orchester again.

updateFailed.title: Orchester couldn't update its data
updateFailed.reason: Updating the database to this version would leave {{count}} broken references, so it was left unchanged.
updateFailed.description: It has data version {{found}}; this build needs version {{supported}}.
updateFailed.step: Start the previous Orchester version to keep working with this data, and report the problem with the log.

notWritable.title: Orchester can't write to its data folder
notWritable.besideProgram: Orchester keeps its data beside its program, and your account can't write to this folder.
notWritable.elsewhere: Orchester keeps its data in this folder, and your account can't write to it.
notWritable.stepBesideProgram: Install Orchester in a folder your account can write to, or give your account write access to this one.
notWritable.stepElsewhere: Check that your account owns this folder and can write to it, then start Orchester again.

programFolder.title: Orchester can't find its own folder
programFolder.reason: The folder of the Orchester program could not be determined.
programFolder.description: Orchester keeps its data and its runner beside its program, so it can't open them. The log has the system's reason.
programFolder.step: Start Orchester from its install folder, or install it again.

agentCli.title: {{program}} isn't found on this computer
agentCli.bodyLoginShell: Apps started from Finder don't get your terminal's PATH. Orchester read it from your login shell ({{shell}}) and still can't find {{program}}. Local projects open; agents can't start until it's found.
agentCli.bodyUsualFolders: Orchester looked on your PATH and in the usual install folders and can't find {{program}}. Local projects open; agents can't start until it's found.
agentCli.bodyPath: Orchester looked in the folders on your PATH and can't find {{program}}. Local projects open; agents can't start until it's found.
agentCli.noFolders: There are no folders on PATH to look in.

join.title: Join a team
join.lead: Two ways in. Either one gives this computer its own sign-in on the team server; nothing local is uploaded.
join.note: Orchester Cloud is only for team features. Without it, local projects work as before.

cloud.title: With Orchester Cloud
cloud.sub: Lists every team and invite of your account

code.title: With a code
code.sub: For a team server without the internet, or without Cloud
code.label: Code
code.hint: An invite code from a teammate, or a pairing code from your other computer. 8 characters, works once.
code.wrong: Wrong or expired. A code works once, within 10 minutes: ask for a new one.

unreachable.title: Can't reach {{host}}
unreachable.body: No answer in {{seconds}} seconds. Check the address and your network, or ask the team's owner if the server is running.

settings.title: {{server}} needs a check first
settings.body: Its certificate or plain HTTP needs your check. Join it in Settings › Orchester › Connect a server.

teams.title: Choose a team
teams.lead: The team servers and invites of your Orchester Cloud account. Joining gives this computer its own sign-in there.
teams.none: No team servers in your account yet.
teams.notListed: A team not listed? Ask its owner to invite {{email}}, or join with a code.

joined.title: Joined {{server}} as {{username}}
joined.body: This computer has its own sign-in there now.

waiting.title: Waiting for approval
waiting.body: {{server}} asks for approval of new computers. Approve this one on another computer of yours, or ask an admin. Nothing has been uploaded.

notInvited.title: {{server}} has no place for {{email}}
notInvited.body: Ask its owner to invite this email, or join with a code.
